name: Sales transactions
summary: Point-of-sale checks, e-commerce orders or order lines: what sold, when, through which channel and location, and what came off for discounts, refunds, tax and tips.

goals.label: See what's selling
goals.desc: I'd break sales down by product, day and channel

goals.label: Find leaks
goals.desc: I'd total refunds, voids, comps and discounts

goals.label: Bring customers back
goals.desc: I'd find regulars who stopped ordering

goals.label: Tune the menu or catalog
goals.desc: I'd rank items by sales and margin

questions.prompt: When you say sales, what does that number leave out? Pick all that apply.

options.label: Discounts
options.desc: Discounts are left out of sales

options.label: Refunds
options.desc: Refunds are left out of sales

questions.why: Every total, trend and average rests on one definition of a sale.

fact.statement: Sales, as the owner counts them, leave out: {answer_labels}.

questions.prompt: There are {rows} rows and {count:order_id} different values in {role:order_id}. Is each row one item on an order, one whole order, or one payment?
questions.why: Adding up a total that repeats on every item line counts the same order many times.

fact.statement: One row in this sheet is, per the owner: {answer_labels}.

questions.prompt: Which orders should stay out of sales? Pick all that apply.

options.label: Voided orders
options.desc: Voided orders stay out of sales

options.label: Test orders
options.desc: Test orders stay out of sales

options.label: Wholesale orders
options.desc: Wholesale orders stay out of sales

questions.why: A few test or voided orders can move averages, and one bulk order can make a normal week look like a record.

fact.statement: The owner said to leave these out of sales: {answer_labels}.

questions.prompt: Which date does a sale belong to?

options.label: The business day
options.desc: Late-night sales count to the day before

questions.why: Daily and weekly totals shift depending on which date is used.

fact.statement: A sale belongs to this date, per the owner: {answer_labels}.

questions.prompt: {role:tax} adds up to {sum:tax} on {rows:tax} rows. Do prices in {role:unit_price} already include sales tax?

options.label: No, tax is added on top
Yes, tax is inside the price

questions.recommend_basis: In the US, menu and shelf prices usually exclude sales tax, which is added at checkout.
questions.why: Tax inside prices inflates sales and every per-item average.

fact.statement: Tax treatment of {role:unit_price}, per the owner: {answer_labels}.

questions.prompt: {role:customer_email} has {count:customer_email} different addresses on {rows:customer_email} rows. Should orders with the same {role:customer_email} count as one customer?
questions.why: Repeat rates and the win-back list depend on knowing who came back.

fact.statement: Orders sharing the same {role:customer_email}, per the owner: {answer_labels}.

questions.prompt: Do sales through the {count:channel} channels in {role:channel}, such as {values:channel}, cost you a commission or fee beyond card processing?

options.label: Yes, delivery apps take a cut

questions.why: A delivery-app order at the same price can earn far less than a direct or dine-in order.

fact.statement: Fees on sales by channel, per the owner: {answer_labels}.

questions.prompt: To rank items by margin I need what each one costs. Where does that live?

options.label: I'll type costs for top items

questions.why: Popularity alone ranks a best seller that loses money above a quieter item that earns it.

fact.statement: Item costs come from, per the owner: {answer_labels}.

questions.prompt: How long without an order before a customer counts as lapsed?
questions.why: The win-back list is only as good as the line between a regular and a lost customer.

fact.statement: A customer counts as lapsed after this long without an order, per the owner: {answer_labels}.

outputs.title: Sales picture
outputs.pitch: Sales picture: sales by week, product, channel and location, with average order size and items per order.

outputs.title: Leak report
outputs.pitch: Leak report: refunds, voids, comps, discounts and channel fees totaled by week, item and location, with the biggest outliers named.

outputs.title: Win-back list
outputs.pitch: Win-back list: regular customers who have not ordered in a while, ranked by what they used to spend, saved as a new file.

outputs.title: Menu and product mix
outputs.pitch: Menu and product mix: connect a recipe cost or purchase file on product or SKU and rank every item by sales and margin.

outputs.title: Guide for the next owner
outputs.pitch: Guide for the next owner: a plain page on what one row is, what counts as a sale here, which orders are left out and how the totals tie to the books.

outputs.title: App blueprint
outputs.pitch: App blueprint: a daily sales digest that reads each day's export and writes up yesterday's sales, leaks and top movers in one short note.

gotchas.say: {role:total} may repeat the whole order's total on every item line, or appear only on the first line, so adding it line by line can count one order many times.
{role:net_sales} has negative rows: refunds or voids recorded as their own lines.
{role:tip} is money for staff, not revenue, so totals that include it overstate sales.
{role:tax} is collected for the state, not earned, so sales figures usually leave it out.
This table has more than one date column, and a sale can land on a different day depending on which one is used.
{role:refund} can land weeks after the original sale, so one week's refunds may belong to earlier weeks' orders.
{role:category} is blank on some rows; open-price items, fees and gift cards often carry no category.
{role:discount} can mix promotions with comps. Comps are items given away by staff; promotions are offers to customers.
Online exports often stamp times in UTC, so late-evening sales can fall on the next calendar day.
{role:channel} splits sales into {values:channel}; delivery-app orders often carry commissions the sales figure does not show.

graph.sentence: Dots are products, categories, channels and locations. Customers appear when records are turned on. Lines show what sells where. Bigger means more sales.

rules.basis: Menu and catalog prices usually change a few times a year.
